criteria.criterion: Turn 1 asks for or plans workload classification by criticality and migratability
criteria.evidence: Migratability is covered well: "Check for VMs with pinned CPUs, SR-IOV, passthrough GPUs, or local-disk... These often can't live-migrate, so plan cold migrations or downtime with their owners" and "Do you have any non-migratable VMs (GPU, SR-IOV, pinned)?". Criticality is only implied by "Notify teams with non-migratable or latency-sensitive VMs". The response never sets out classification by business criticality as a planning step.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 bounds batches by spare capacity per AZ and handles SR-IOV, GPU and the DB cluster differently
criteria.evidence: "With about 2 hosts of spare capacity per AZ, you can drain at most 2 hosts at once... run 1 host at a time by default". GPU VMs: "stop, patch host, start on the same host". SR-IOV VMs get the same treatment "unless you've verified your Nova/libvirt version supports live migration for them", plus owner sign-off. DB cluster: "Never have two of its hosts down at the same time... Pin those hosts into separate batches", with a tenant health check between steps.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 or earlier defines stop conditions before the campaign continues
criteria.evidence: Turn 1 sets go/no-go gates and "stop if more than 1 host fails". Turn 2 repeats it: "Migration failure rate stays low. Stop after 1 failed host." It also adds gates for Ceph HEALTH_OK, remaining capacity and DB cluster health.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 treats the failed migration as a stop condition and does not continue to cmp-a-06
criteria.evidence: "No, pause. This is the stop condition we set (stop after 1 failed host)." It explains that a systemic cause would make cmp-a-06 fail the same way.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 starts with read-only checks of where the VM runs and why the migration failed
criteria.evidence: "Don't touch the VM yet. Do not reboot it, reset-state it, or delete it. First find out where it really is." It then gives read-only checks: server show, virsh list and ps on both hosts, nova-compute, libvirt/QEMU and conductor logs, and migration list/show. State-changing recovery comes only afterwards.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 makes resuming a new decision with owner involvement
criteria.evidence: Before resuming, it requires clean RBD locks and a healthy VM "with the owner's confirmation". A hard reboot needs "check with the owner first". A separate section, "Deciding how to proceed", splits the one-off case from the systemic case and asks "Who owns this VM?". Weakness: in the one-off case it says "continue as planned", and the reset-state option has no named approver.

critical_errors.error: in turn 3, says to carry on with the next host before understanding the failure
critical_errors.evidence: "No, pause... Fix this first." It continues only after the cause is classified as one-off or systemic.
It uses live migration (`nova host-evacuate-live`), cold migration, or stop/start in place. Plain `nova evacuate` is never recommended.

critical_errors.error: proposes reset-state or other state-changing fixes on the VM without first establishing where it runs
critical_errors.evidence: Step 1 explicitly forbids reset-state before locating the VM. `server set --state active` is offered only "If it's running fine on the source... after you confirm the guest is actually running".

critical_errors.error: plans live migration of GPU passthrough VMs as if supported
critical_errors.evidence: "SR-IOV (6 VMs) and GPU passthrough (2 VMs) can't be live-migrated in most setups". GPU VMs are stopped and started in place.

summary: This is a strong response across all three turns, and it commits none of the critical errors. Turn 2 bounds batches by the roughly 2 spare hosts per AZ and gives SR-IOV, GPU passthrough and the DB cluster separate methods. Stop conditions are set before the campaign starts. In turn 3 the assistant stops the campaign, forbids state changes until the VM's location is established, lists read-only checks and logs to read, and requires owner confirmation before resuming. Two weaknesses: turn 1 covers migratability but only weakly addresses business criticality, and the turn 3 resume path in the one-off case ("continue as planned") has no named approver beyond the VM owner. There are no book citations and no invented environment facts.
